text_blocks.snippet: Yellow mucus can be an indicator of a viral or bacterial infection, as it often signifies the presence of white blood cells fighting off pathogens. While it's not a definitive sign of a specific type of infection, it suggests the body's immune system is actively engaged in combating something. Other causes, such as allergies or environmental irritants, can also lead to yellow mucus.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yellow mucus can be an indicator of a viral or bacterial infection

list.title: Infection:
list.snippet: Yellow mucus is a common sign of a viral or bacterial infection, like the common cold or sinusitis. The color change is due to white blood cells (like neutrophils) accumulating in the mucus as they fight off the infection, and these cells can turn the mucus yellow or green.

list.title: Allergies:
list.snippet: Allergies can also cause mucus to change color, sometimes to a yellow tinge, especially as the condition worsens or if a secondary infection develops.

list.title: Non-infectious causes:
list.snippet: Environmental factors like smoke, pollution, or dust can irritate the nasal passages and cause mucus production, potentially leading to yellow or discolored mucus.
